exposure: Low 50-g, 1-hour glucose challenge test (GCT) value (defined as cohort specific ≤10(th) percentile (<82 mg/dL))
outcome: Composite neonatal morbidity (stillbirth, neonatal death, neonatal hypoglycemia with NICU admission, neonatal hyperbilirubinemia with NICU admission, respiratory distress with NICU admission, and/or small for gestational age (SGA))
cohort: 36,342 pregnant patients with a documented result of a 50-gram, 1-hour GCT performed ≥24 weeks 0 days gestation at a single tertiary care academic hospital from 2013-2021.
finding: A low maternal GCT value after 24 weeks gestation is significantly associated with an increased risk of composite neonatal morbidity, primarily driven by higher rates of SGA, even after adjusting for potential confounders.
